modelResponse.episodeSummary: 70yo M with ESRD, symptomatic bradycardia and hypotension, presenting with third-degree AV block.
keyECGEvidence: AV dissociation; wide QRS escape; tall peaked symmetric T waves; flattened P waves
Progressive PR prolongation then AV dissociation; QRS widening over 20 min
modelResponse.mechanism: Hyperkalemia causes slowed conduction through the AV node and His-Purkinje system, leading to progressive PR prolongation, QRS widening, and eventually complete AV dissociation and ventricular escape rhythms.
contributingFactors: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) with missed hemodialysis
Metabolic acidosis (pH 7.24 LOW, bicarbonate 15 mmol/L LOW)

rejectedAlternatives.why: The presence of 'tall peaked symmetric T waves' and 'K 7.4 mmol/L CRITICAL HIGH' strongly points to metabolic etiology rather than primary nodal disease.
While it can cause AV block and wide QRS, there is no mention of digoxin use in the patient's medication list.

recommendedActions: Urgent emergent hemodialysis to treat K 7.4 mmol/L CRITICAL HIGH and ESRD
Administer intravenous Calcium Gluconate (or Calcium Chloride) to stabilize cardiac membranes
Administer intravenous Insulin with Dextrose (to shift potassium intracellularly)
Administer Albuterol nebulization (to shift potassium intracellularly)
Prepare for transcutaneous or permanent pacing if hemodynamics do not stabilize with medical management
